title: POC weekly readout - benchmark vs incumbent (EdenWell)
summary: Weekly POC readout comparing Redwood inference latency/throughput vs incumbent. Redwood shows better median p50 token latency on targeted prompt set after KV prefix caching + quantization, throughput improved with batch tuning. Discussed dedicated slot for final stress run, security docs, and commercial next steps.

dedicated slot request for final run

What changes are non-intrusive for our infra team?
How will caching affect cold-starts and multi-tenant isolation?

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-02
Start: 2026-09-02T15:00:00Z
Duration: 47 minutes
Location: Zoom
Shared artifacts: Benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.internal/bench/edenwell-0902), Readout deck (link: https://redwood.internal/decks/edenwell-poc-readout.pdf)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM), Dana Morales (EdenWell Head of ML), Samir Gupta (EdenWell Platform Eng), Lena Ortiz (EdenWell Procurement), Priya Narayan (EdenWell SRE)

[00:00:10] Alex Chen: alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. uh quick roll call — if you could just confirm who you are?
[00:00:20] Dana Morales: Hey Dana here, ready.
[00:00:22] Samir Gupta: Samir here.
[00:00:24] Lena Ortiz: Lena on procurement, hi.
[00:00:26] Priya Narayan: Priya SRE, hi all.
[00:00:30] Alex Chen: great. So agenda, well run through the weeks benchmark readout, recon the tuning we did (batching, quantize profile, KV prefix caching), then lay out next steps for the dedicated run and security artifacts.

[00:02:05] Maya Patel: quick framing — we re-ran the same prompt set you provided last week (the "clinical-summaries-v2" set), matched the baseline request distribution, and ran on Redwood Dedicated slot with the 24GB GPU profile we discussed. we also toggled quantize LLM to int4 and enabled prefix KV cache for repeated recent tokens.

[00:03:10] Samir Gupta: Can you remind us what the incumbent numbers were? Our SRE ran earlier baseline on IncumbentCloudAI last friday.
[00:03:20] Alex Chen: sure; per the spreadsheet row "Baseline-ICAI-2026-08-28": median per-token latency p50 = 18ms, p95 token latency around 65ms, end-to-end generation p50 for our prompt set about 420ms, p95 about 1.2s. throughput wise they peaked at ~650 tokens/s on your instance size during synthetic parallel runs.

[00:04:00] Dana Morales: that sounds right. what did Redwood get?
[00:04:05] Maya Patel: after tuning: p50 token latency ~12-13ms, p95 token latency ~48-52ms, end-to-end p50 ~320ms, p95 ~880ms. throughput steady at 820 tokens/s under our 4-worker config with continuous batching. so roughly 20-30% improvement on median latency and higher throughput.

[00:05:12] Priya Narayan: those numbers look promising, but curious about the measurement noise. did you run multiple runs or just single snapshot?
[00:05:22] Maya Patel: multiple runs — we did 3 replicate runs per config, each run 10 minutes with the same traffic replay. we also did a cold-start run to measure cache warming: cold-start p50 was closer to 18ms token, which matches incumbent for cold paths, but warm path wins thanks to KV prefix cache.

[00:06:10] Samir Gupta: when you say KV prefix cache, is that per-tenant or global multi-tenant? we do not want cross-tenant leakage.
[00:06:20] Maya Patel: good call — it's per-customer isolate, so the cache is keyed by customer namespace. there was a slight mislabel in the doc but it's tenant-scoped. also cache TTL is configurable; in our run we used a 30 minute TTL to capture repeated conversational prefixes.

[00:07:00] Dana Morales: what about memory overhead? our GPUs are tight on 24GB instances.
[00:07:06] Maya Patel: quantization to int4 saved about 28% memory on the model params, allowing bigger batch sizes. KV cache uses about 1.2GB per 1M tokens in active cache in our measurements, so it's modest. we also offload some KV to host RAM if GPU pressure hits a threshold.

[00:08:35] Alex Chen: we had one run where p95 spiked to 1.5s, that was during a background GC on the host node — we marked it as an outlier in the spreadsheet.

[00:09:00] Samir Gupta: interesting. Are these runs reproducible in our environment? wed like to run the same harness.
[00:09:08] Maya Patel: yes — we pushed the exact runbook and scripts to the bench spreadsheet link, plus docker image tags, and a small infra playbook for VPC peering and kube config. we'll share the raw CSVs.

[00:10:40] Lena Ortiz: procurement question: if we want a dedicated slot for the final stress run, whats the lead time and cost?
[00:10:50] Alex Chen: lead time is typically 5 business days to provision a dedicated pool in your selected region for a short-term reserved slot. cost we estimate on the bench spreadsheet (column "dedicated-est"); Jordan will send a formal quote.

[00:11:30] Jordan Li: Ill follow up with pricing and the templated contract language. For a one-week dedicated stress window, we can do a short-term reservation at a discounted pilot rate.

[00:12:10] Dana Morales: security — did you run includes around SSO and audit logs? we need to show SOC2 evidence to our compliance folks.
[00:12:20] Jordan Li: yes, SOC2 Type II report available. also we have audit log retention options and KMS integration — I'll send the links after the call.

[00:13:05] Priya Narayan: networking — we prefer VPC peering to allow our SREs to send load generators from our subnet. any caveats?
[00:13:13] Maya Patel: VPC peering is standard. if you want on-prem / air-gapped we also have a private deployment product but thats a bigger lift. For this POC, peering + mutual TLS should be straightforward. we have a network checklist (we'll attach).

[00:14:40] Samir Gupta: how did you tune batching? we saw some jitter when we increased max-batch-size.
[00:14:48] Maya Patel: we adjust batch window and max batch size together: for this workload we set max-batch-size = 32, batch-wait = 8ms, and token scheduling prioritized low-latency interactive requests. that gave best p50 while keeping throughput high. if you push for max throughput we can increase batch size but p95 will go up.

[00:15:30] Dana Morales: can we see the knob sensitivity? like if we move batch-wait to 12ms what happens?
[00:15:36] Maya Patel: yes, we've got a sensitivity sheet in the spreadsheet; 12ms nudges p50 ~+2ms but increases throughput by ~7%.

[00:16:10] Alex Chen: quick interruption — there's a note on the deck about fallback routing: when capacity constrained, Redwood can fall back to a smaller quantized model; that keeps availability but may affect output quality.

[00:16:30] Priya Narayan: so fallback could route to different model family — how do you guarantee deterministic outputs for auditing?
[00:16:38] Maya Patel: good question; we tag model versions and maintain lineage in the rollout logs. audit logs record the exact model-id and quantization profile used for each request.

[00:17:50] Samir Gupta: we noticed one config you used: "kv-prefix-ttl=30m". what if we set TTL to 5m?
[00:17:58] Maya Patel: TTL tradeoff: lower TTL reduces stale reuse but increases cold-starts. for highly dynamic sessions we recommend 5-10m. for multi-turn clinical dialogs 30m was best.

[00:19:10] Dana Morales: any limitations with our current infra? Priya?
[00:19:15] Priya Narayan: main concern is network egress during stress runs; need to schedule with infra team. also want the exact run scripts so we can vet them.

[00:20:00] Alex Chen: we'll provide the run scripts and a pre-provision checklist.

[00:21:30] Maya Patel: i want to call out a weird artifact in one of your trace sessions: some prompts had long prefix repeats which inflated throughput on incumbent because they cached across tenants — we removed those repeats for fair comparison. that explained a 10% discrepancy in one run.

[00:22:20] Samir Gupta: thanks for cleaning that. on quality side, did you surface any regression in generation with int4 quantize?
[00:22:28] Maya Patel: we ran an eval set; ROUGE and clinical-entity F1 were within 1.5% of float baseline for int4 in our tests. we flagged a small hallucination in one prompt, but that was replicated on incumbent too.

[00:23:45] Dana Morales: ok. what's the ask from our side to get the dedicated stress run?
[00:23:50] Alex Chen: two things: 1) provide a representative traffic trace (Samir/Dana) 2) confirm a 72-hour window where your team can accept peering and test traffic. after that we provision the dedicated pool and run the stress script.

[00:24:12] Lena Ortiz: procurement will need a short MOU for the dedicated slot, and a cost estimate to sign off.

[00:24:30] Jordan Li: Ill send the MOU and cost estimate by end of week.

[00:25:40] Maya Patel: quick demo share-screen moment — showing p50/p95 charts from the bench spreadsheet.
[00:25:50] (screen share)
[00:26:10] Maya Patel: see this plot: p95 reduces after we enable prefix cache and switch to int4. the blue is incumbent, orange is Redwood run.

[00:27:00] Dana Morales: are those boxplots from 3 runs?
[00:27:05] Maya Patel: yes, aggregated. we also show per-run CSV below.

[00:28:15] Samir Gupta: curious about tail latency under sustained parallel load; can you replicate 1k parallel users?
[00:28:24] Maya Patel: we can, but that's where dedicated slot matters — multi-tenant hosted sometimes throttles. for 1k parallel users we recommend the dedicated pool sized at least N=6 GPUs (we estimated N=4-8 in sheet).

[00:29:40] Priya Narayan: what about observability hooks? we need traces in our tracing system.
[00:29:48] Alex Chen: we support open telemetry exports; we can push traces to your collector or provide S3 export of logs.

[00:30:35] Dana Morales: any vendor lock risks if we roll out with Redwood?
[00:30:40] Alex Chen: we try to be transparent: you can pin model versions and export key artifacts. if you need an on-prem bundle later, we have Redwood Private option.

[00:31:50] Samir Gupta: small nit — in the bench spreadsheet the GPU type was ECS-rtx-a6000, we actually run on A100s in prod. will numbers change?
[00:32:00] Maya Patel: A100s will improve throughput and slightly reduce token latency. we can re-run on A100 profile during the dedicated stress window to provide apples-to-apples comparison.

[00:33:30] Alex Chen: recap before action items: Redwood shows a consistent median and higher throughput compared to incumbent for your prompt set when warm caching and int4 quantimen enabled. cold-starts are similar. next is dedicated stress run, share artifacts, and prod trace.

[00:34:10] Lena Ortiz: ok procurement will await Jordans quote.
[00:34:20] Jordan Li: sending quote + MOU by Friday.

[00:35:05] Dana Morales: any remaining risks we should call out?
[00:35:10] Maya Patel: main risks: network egress, cold-start for rare prompts, and model-quality regressions for very narrow clinical templates — we recommend a final eval set for quality gating.

[00:36:00] Priya Narayan: will look at the run scripts and sign off on network.

[00:37:20] Alex Chen: great. let's confirm dates: we propose the dedicated window week of 2026-09-14. does that work?
[00:37:27] Dana Morales: yes that week looks good.
[00:37:30] Samir Gupta: ok.

[00:38:00] Alex Chen: final housekeeping: i've added the raw CSV and command lines in the shared bench link. Jordan will send legal and cost. Maya will schedule the reserved slot. Jordan will send SOC2 link.

[00:39:20] Lena Ortiz: one ask — include a one-page latency explainers we can show to execs.
[00:39:28] Alex Chen: will do.

[00:40:00] (small cross talk)
[00:41:10] Maya Patel: quick note on reproducibility: we pinned docker image tag rwd-infer:2026-08-30, and included the seed for the traffic generator.

[00:42:05] Dana Morales: that's good. thanks everyone.
[00:42:10] Alex Chen: thanks all, well follow up with next steps.
[00:42:20] Jordan Li: meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
